reason: Conversation 1 correctly identified the clogged condenser as the most likely cause, gave accurate step-by-step removal and rinsing instructions (unlock levers, rinse through fins, clean the cavity and seals), flagged the fabric-softener film on the filter and sensor bars, and then used the 20-minute hot-drum test to confirm the heater was fine and no parts were needed, finishing with sensible maintenance intervals. Conversation 2 reached the same outcome but misidentified the WTN85201GB as a 'heat-pump dryer', gave vaguer access instructions ('pull it straight out', 'drip-dry for 10 minutes') that never actually told the customer to rinse the condenser, and closed without confirming heating or giving concrete maintenance intervals. Conversation 1's only weaknesses are length and a premature but clearly conditional mention of heater/thermostat testing with an engineer alternative; neither conversation explicitly said to unplug before removing the condenser.
